extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of political philosophy and law; readers of Hobbes' Leviathan; those studying governance, sovereignty, and constitutional theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes Hobbes' principles on the structure and functioning of commonwealths: representation, assemblies, public ministers, property, trade, and money. Useful for analyzing or applying Hobbesian rules about sovereignty, obligations, and institutional limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts of an Assembly bind only assenting members
rubrics_metrics.description: That whatsoever debt is by that Assembly contracted; or whatsoever unlawfull Act is decreed, is the Act onely of those that assented, and not of any that dissented, or were absent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the moral/legal scope of assembly acts: liability and responsibility attach only to those who voted for or assisted in execution; dissenters/absentees are not bound for reasons previously alleged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly residing outside colony has no jurisdiction beyond colony
rubrics_metrics.description: An Assembly residing out of the bounds of that Colony whereof they have the government, cannot execute any power over the persons, or goods of any of the Colonie ... in any place without the Colony it selfe, as having no Jurisdiction, nor Authoritie elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such extraterritorial enforcement is impermissible; remedies are left to the law of the place where the person or goods are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemblies can fine members but cannot enforce fines extraterritorially
rubrics_metrics.description: Though the Assembly have right, to impose a Mulct upon any of their members, that shall break the Lawes they make; yet out of the Colonie it selfe, they have no right to execute the same
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement of internal penalties is limited to the geographical bounds of the political community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of provincial assemblies apply to towns, universities, churches etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: That which is said here, of the Rights of an Assembly, for the government of a Province, or a Colony, is appliable also to an Assembly for the Government of a Town, or University, or a College, or a Church
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same principles about representation, jurisdiction, and binding acts are scalable to varied corporate bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disputes between a member and the body belong to the sovereign's cognisance
rubrics_metrics.description: If any particular member conceive himself Injured by the Body it self, the Cognisance of his cause belongeth to the Soveraign, and those the Soveraign hath ordained for Judges ... and not to the Body it self
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The body is, in such cases, treated as a fellow-subject; only the sovereign (or judges appointed by the sovereign) may adjudicate such internal grievances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where sovereign is not judge there can be no judge at all
rubrics_metrics.description: For the whole Body is in this case his fellow subject, which in a Soveraign Assembly, is otherwise: for there, if the Soveraign be not Judge, though in his own cause, there can be no Judge at all
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes indivisibility of ultimate judicial authority in the sovereign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative structure for foreign trade should allow all adventurers presence
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Bodie Politique, for the well ordering of forraigne Traffique, the most commodious Representative is an Assembly of all the members; that is to say, such a one, as every one that adventureth his mony, may be present at all the Deliberations, and Resolutions of the Body
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because merchants bind themselves corporately for trade, the representative body that governs foreign trade ought to permit any investor to participate in deliberations to safeguard their particular gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merchant corporations as double monopolies and their harms
rubrics_metrics.description: To grant to a Company of Merchants to be a Corporation, or Body Politique, is to grant them a double Monopoly, whereof one is to be sole buyers; another to be sole sellers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains economic consequences: at home they set prices on native goods; abroad they act as sole sellers, disadvantaging foreigners; such corporations are profitable to merchants but harmful to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative of merchant body must be an assembly with open participation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is reason that every one be acquainted with the employment of his own; that is, that every one be of the Assembly, that shall have the power to order the same; and be acquainted with their accounts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The governance of a trading corporation should be transparent and participatory for each adventurer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for corporate debts to strangers attaches to each member individually
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Body Politique of Merchants, contract a debt to a stranger by the act of their Representative Assembly, every Member is lyable by himself for the whole
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stranger cannot know private corporate laws and treats members as jointly liable until payment discharges all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debts owed to one within the company are enforceable only from common stock
rubrics_metrics.description: But if the debt be to one of the Company, the creditor is debter for the whole to himself, and cannot therefore demand his debt, but only from the common stock, if there be any
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal creditors must rely on the corporate fund rather than individual member liability in this case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes on a corporate body are apportioned to members by adventure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Common-wealth impose a Tax upon the Body, it is understood to be layd upon every member proportionably to his particular adventure in the Company
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no other common stock beyond aggregated individual adventures used to apportion public levies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fines on a body attach only to those whose votes or assistance caused the unlawful act
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Mulct be layd upon the Body for some unlawfull act, they only are lyable by whose votes the act was decreed, or by whose assistance it was executed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members not involved in decision or execution bear no guilt beyond mere membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: A corporate body cannot imprison or seize by its own authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If one of the Members be indebted to the Body, he may be sued by the Body; but his goods cannot be taken, nor his person imprisoned by the authority of the Body; but only by Authority of the Common-wealth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A body has no judicial or coercive power to enforce judgments that would make it judge in its own cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deputy assemblies summoned by sovereign represent subjects only for specified matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Such Deputies, having a place and time of meeting assigned them, are there, and at that time, a Body Politique ... but it is onely for such matters as shall be propounded unto them by that Man, or Assembly, that by the Soveraign Authority sent for them
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope and duration of such representative bodies are defined by the sovereign's writ; they cannot act beyond those limits without creating multiple sovereignties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private regular bodies (families) are lawful and hierarchical under commonwealth law
rubrics_metrics.description: Private Bodies Regular, and Lawfull, are those that are constituted without Letters ... because they be united in one Person Representative, they are held for Regular; such as are all Families, in which the Father, or Master ordereth the whole Family
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family heads retain domestic authority so far as the common law permits; they lose only what the law of the commonwealth takes from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private regular but unlawful bodies (criminal corporations) are illegitimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Private Bodies Regular, but Unlawfull, are those that unite themselves into one person Representative, without any publique Authority at all; such as are the Corporations of Beggars, Theeves and Gipsies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations formed without public sanction that pursue unlawful ends are excluded from legitimate corporate status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leagues and irregular systems lawfulness depends on members' designs and occasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Irregular Systemes ... become Lawfull, or Unlawfull, according to the lawfulnesse, or unlawfulnesse of every particular mans design therein
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leagues between sovereign commonwealths are generally lawful and profitable; leagues among subjects of one commonwealth are unnecessary or unlawful, especially if secret or with evil design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret cabals within assemblies constitute unlawful factions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Soveraign Power be in a great Assembly, and a number of men, part of the Assembly, without authority, consult a part, to contrive the guidance of the rest; This is a Faction, or Conspiracy unlawfull
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covert coordination to subvert assembly decisions is fraudulent; but soliciting friends when one's private interest is to be debated is not unjust (unless explicitly prohibited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Private arming and hosting of excessive retainers is factional and unlawful
rubrics_metrics.description: If a private man entertain more servants, than the government of his estate, and lawfull employment he has for them requires, it is Faction, and unlawfull
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private forces, beyond household needs, threaten public peace and usurp the sovereign's monopoly on force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemblies/concourses lawfulness judged by occasion and manageable size
rubrics_metrics.description: Concourse of people, is an Irregular Systeme, the lawfulnesse, or unlawfulnesse, whereof dependeth on the occasion, and on the number of them that are assembled
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinary public gatherings (church, public show) are lawful; extraordinarily large assemblies without evident occasion are tumultuous and may be judged seditious. The appropriate number is one that present officers can control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public ministers are those employed by sovereign to represent the commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: A PUBLIQUE MINISTER, is he, that by the Soveraign ... is employed in any affaires, with Authority to represent in that employment, the Person of the Common-wealth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes public ministers from household officers (ushers, sergeants, stewards), who serve natural capacities rather than the commonwealth's political person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers for general administration derive authority from sovereign and cannot transfer sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: Such Protectors, Vice-Roys, and Governours have no other right, but what depends on the Soveraigns Will; and no Commission that can be given them, can be interpreted for a Declaration of the will to transferre the Soverignty, without expresse and perspicuous words to that purpose
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegated governors may bind subjects within their commission but cannot alter the ultimate sovereignty absent explicit language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers of finance are public when they manage public treasure and revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: They that have Authority concerning the Treasure, as Tributes, Impositions, Rents, Fines, or whatsoever publique revenue, to collect, receive, issue, or take the Accounts thereof, are Publique Ministers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal officers represent the sovereign in administering commonwealth resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military and defense officers are public ministers with command responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: They that have Authority concerning the Militia; to have the custody of Armes, Forts, Ports; to Levy, Pay, or Conduct Souldiers ... are publique Ministers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those with command represent the person of the commonwealth; a soldier without command does not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teachers of civic duty are public ministers when authorized by sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: They also that have authority to teach, or to enable others to teach the people their duty to the Soveraign Power ... are Publique Ministers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign holds the immediate authority to teach; all other instructional authority derives from the sovereign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges represent sovereign; judicature essentially annexed to sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: They also to whom Jurisdiction is given, are Publique Ministers. For in their Seats of Justice they represent the person of the Soveraign; and their Sentence, is his Sentence ... all Judicature is essentially annexed to the Soveraignty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes judgments of fact and law; procedures for exceptions and appeals are framed so parties can agree on judges or appeal to sovereign whose sentence is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public ministers execute judgments and preserve peace
rubrics_metrics.description: Publique Ministers are also all those, that have Authority from the Soveraign, to procure the Execution of Judgements given; to publish the Soveraigns Commands; to suppresse Tumults; to apprehend, and imprison Malefactors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Execution and enforcement are public acts representing the commonwealth, comparable to organs effecting bodily motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambassadors and envoys abroad represent the sovereign as public ministers
rubrics_metrics.description: Publique Ministers abroad, are those that represent the Person of their own Soveraign, to forraign States. Such are Ambassadors, Messengers, Agents, and Heralds, sent by publique Authoritie, and on publique Businesse
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents without public authority, or sent by private parties, do not have actions attributable to the commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsellors who only advise are not public ministers
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither a Counsellor, nor a Councell of State, if we consider it with no Authority of Judicature or Command, but only of giving Advice ... is a Publique Person
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice alone does not constitute representation of the sovereign; councils normally possess some additional judicial or administrative authority to be public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nutrition of commonwealth depends on plenty, preparation, and conveyance of commodities
rubrics_metrics.description: The NUTRITION of a Common-wealth consisteth, in the Plenty, and Distribution of Materials conducing to Life: In Concoction, or Preparation; and (when concocted) in the Conveyance of it, by convenient conduits, to the Publique use
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'matter' (commodities) as native and foreign; plenty depends on labour and industry; trade and manufacture can increase power even with limited territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution (property) belongs to the sovereign and originates private estates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Distribution of the Materials of this Nourishment ... belongeth in all kinds of Common-wealth to the Soveraign Power ... All Private Estates Of Land Proceed Originally From The Arbitrary Distribution Of The Soveraign
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propriety (mine/thine) is an effect of commonwealth law; sovereign allocates land and property rights, which subjects hold as derived from sovereign distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private property excludes other subjects but not sovereign dominion
rubrics_metrics.description: the Propriety which a subject hath in his lands, consisteth in a right to exclude all other subjects from the use of them; and not to exclude their Soveraign
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject's property rights operate within the continued supremacy of sovereign authority; sovereign may alter distributions under public purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning a fixed portion ('diet') to the public is vain and unstable
rubrics_metrics.description: The Publique Is Not To Be Dieted ... the setting forth of Publique Land, or of any certaine Revenue for the Common-wealth, is in vaine; and tendeth to the dissolution of Government
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public revenues cannot be safely fixed because representatives may alienate or mismanage them; emergent needs make fixed maintenance unrealistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign controls places and matter of foreign traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: The Places And Matter Of Traffique Depend, As Their Distribution, On The Soveraign
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign determines where and with what commodities subjects may trade abroad to prevent harms or advantages to enemies and to regulate public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign prescribes laws for transferring property and contract formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: it belongeth to the Common-wealth, (that is to say, to the Soveraign,) to appoint in what manner, all kinds of contract between Subjects ... are to bee made; and by what words, and signes they shall be understood for valid
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign defines legal forms and requirements for valid bargains, exchanges, leases, loans, and other transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money is the concoction (portable store) of commodities; gold and silver are preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: By Concoction, I understand the reducing of all commodities ... to some thing of equal value, and withall so portably ... And this is nothing else but Gold, and Silver, and Mony
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Money functions as circulating nourishment for the commonwealth; gold and silver have advantages as stable, internationally valued measures, while base money is easily debased.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gold and silver have privileges as international measures and for provisioning armies
rubrics_metrics.description: they have first this priviledge, that the value of them cannot be altered by the power of one, nor of a few Common-wealths ... Secondly, they have the priviledge to make Common-wealths, move, and stretch out their armes, when need is, into forraign Countries
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precious metals enable international commerce and military provisioning; their external valuation lends stability that coined money within a commonwealth may lack.
